client: Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce & Industry (SICCI)
seo_title: SICCI Case Study: People-Led Chamber Content | SOMIN
description: Fyreflyz used SOMIN to read 1,820 peer chamber posts for SICCI and found its notices averaged 6 likes while its one post about a person drew 176.
eyebrow: Agency case study · Business chamber · Singapore
h1: SICCI's notices average 6 likes, its one post about a person drew 176
h1_em: its one post about a person drew 176
lede: Fyreflyz used SOMIN to compare 25 posts from the Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce & Industry (SICCI) with 1,820 from six peer chambers over 90 days. SICCI held 1.4% of chamber posts, and the gap showed inside its own feed: notices averaged 6 likes, the one post about a person 176. The pitch builds three people-led series and 36 posts over 12 weeks.
meta_line: A SOMIN agency pitch · 25 Feb to 25 Aug 2026 · Singapore

stats.label: SICCI's share of chamber posts, 90 days
On a post about a person, against 6 for a notice

challenge.title: SICCI's 1.4% share: six peers publish 73 posts to its one
challenge.body: For every post SICCI publishes, its six peer chambers publish 73. In the last 90 days SICCI put out 25 posts, 13 of them unique, most of them notices and event recaps. The pitch had to show that volume was not the only problem, and where SICCI could be heard.

approach.title: SICCI's 25 posts against 1,820 from six peer chambers
points: Compared SICCI's 25 posts with 1,820 posts from six peer chambers (CII, ASME, SICC, SCCCI, SBF and SMCCI) over the last 90 days.
Read six monthly trend windows from Feb to Aug 2026 and checked them against August 2025.
Measured likes per post inside SICCI's own feed by post type: notices, event recaps and posts about a person.
Mapped the themes peers crowd, the ones they own and the ones no chamber covers yet.
Built three SOMIN insight stories, nine propositions and 50 moment triggers to fill the calendar.

findings_title: People posts, crowded India and an untold heritage story

findings.title: People beat notices in the same feed
findings.body: Inside SICCI's own feed, notices averaged 6 likes, event recaps 52 and the one post about a person 176. The peer average is 16.8 engagements per post.

findings.title: India is crowded, the entry story is not
findings.body: India content is 25.1% of peer posts and 44% of SICCI's. CII posts about India 40 times more than SICCI, but it tells India's story, not the story of a Singapore business trying to get in.

findings.title: Heritage is about 4% of peer posts, with no teller
findings.body: Heritage is about 4% of peer posts, yet CII's 'Did you know?' heritage post drew 206 likes and 48 shares, roughly ten times its usual. SICCI has been here since 1924.

delivered.title: Three people-led series, 36 posts and 27 creative concepts
points: Three people-led series: India, one member at a time; the paperwork, explained by people who do it; a hundred years, told by the families who built it
Nine SOMIN propositions for SICCI membership, with the three strongest shown in full
A 12-week calendar from 7 Sep 2026: 36 posts, three a week, 13 lead posts and a Deepavali anchor
27 rendered creative concepts, nine per series across awareness, consideration and conversion
A week-one plan with one measure: likes per post against today's baseline

quote.text: Nobody enters India because of a report. They go because someone they trust already did.

outcome.title: SICCI moves 36 posts from notices to people, tracked by likes
outcome.body: The plan moves 36 posts out of the notices column and into the people column, shot by Fyreflyz's youth crew at 31 Stanley Street. Success is measured one way: likes per post against today's baseline of 6 for notices and 176 for the one people post, reported every Friday.

faq.q: Which chambers was SICCI compared with?
faq.a: Six peer chambers in one SOMIN workspace: CII, ASME, SICC, SCCCI, SBF and SMCCI. Together they published 1,820 posts in the 90-day window, against SICCI's 25.

faq.q: Is the heritage theme confirmed open ground?
faq.a: No. There was no creator panel, so the whitespace read ran in partial mode. 'Who we are and what we built' content is marked possibly open: no chamber is covering it yet, which is a hypothesis to test, not a confirmed gap.

faq.q: How were the creative concepts scored?
faq.a: All 27 rendered creatives were scored in SOMIN for predicted clickability. None reached the 0.80 top-performer bar; the highest, at 35%, came from the people-led India series. These are pre-launch predictions, not results.
